title: The Lord's Prayer: Structure and Glory
speaker: Mr. Nick Newton

outline.title: The Institution of the Lord's Prayer
subpoints: God limits worship to His revealed will (Westminster Confession 21.1)
The Lord's Prayer serves as a template for thoughts, not just words
The primary goal of prayer is the glory of God

outline.title: Structure of the Prayer
subpoints: Consists of three parts: Preface, Petitions, and Conclusion
Prayer requires organized reverence, not casual rambling
Approaching God with an awareness of His holiness and human finitude

outline.title: The First Petition: Hallowed Be Thy Name
subpoints: To regard and treat God's entire revelation as holy
Includes His titles, attributes, ordinances, and Word
Praying for the swift and glorious spread of the Gospel

outline.title: The Second Petition: Thy Kingdom Come
subpoints: Desire for the acceleration of Christ's return
Prayer for the growth of the visible church in numbers and sanctification
Seeking favor from authorities and bold proclamation of the Gospel

outline.title: The Third Petition: Thy Will Be Done
subpoints: Submission to a plan beyond human understanding
Request for grace to overcome sin and live for God's glory

summary: In this Sunday school lesson, Mr. Nick Newton continues the series on the Westminster Larger Catechism, focusing on questions 187 and 188 regarding the use and composition of the Lord's Prayer. The teaching emphasizes that prayer is not merely a list of requests but a structured conversation initiated by God, designed to center His glory above all else. By examining the institution of the prayer in Matthew 6, the lesson highlights that the Lord's Prayer serves as a divine template for the believer's thoughts, ensuring that worship aligns with God's revealed will.
